4. A changing-code operation that is actually available

There is also an exact transport construction.

Suppose

 $H_{\mathcal C}\succeq\frac{\sigma}{N}D_{\mathcal C},$ with check weight at most  $w$  and site incidence at most  $\omega$ . Let  $W$  be an explicitly supplied physical unitary circuit whose forward and backward support expansion is at most  $\ell$ .

Set

 $\mathcal C'=W\mathcal C,\qquad
h_j'=Wh_jW^\dagger.$ Then

 $\boxed{
H_{\mathcal C'}:=WH_{\mathcal C}W^\dagger
\succeq
\frac{\sigma}{\ell N}D_{\mathcal C'}.
}                                                   \tag{6}$ The number of sites and checks is unchanged. Check weight is at most  $w\ell$ , and incidence is at most  $\omega\ell$ .

To prove the energy statement, observe that

 $W\mathcal C_{\le r}\subseteq\mathcal C'_{\le\ell r}.$ Using

 $D_{\mathcal C}=\sum_{r=0}^{N-1}(I-P_r)$ and summing the corresponding projector inequalities gives

 $D_{\mathcal C'}\preceq\ell WD_{\mathcal C}W^\dagger,$ which proves (6).

For depth  $D$  and gate arity  $g_0$ , one can use  $\ell=g_0^D$ . When  $D,w,g_0,d$  are fixed, each new local matrix has fixed dimension. Its lightcone and entries are constructible with polynomial work in the supplied circuit description. Certified approximation followed by the accepted positivity repair charges an additive operator error explicitly.

This operation preserves a storage inequality under bounded-depth physical changes. It does not enforce a transition between an unknown state in one register and an unknown state in another. Independently constraining successive registers to lie in their respective codespaces allows independently chosen logical states.

Likewise, defining a new encoding by

 $V'=WV G^\dagger$ does not implement the logical gate  $G$ . That definition can merely move the computation into the interpretation of the final encoding.

For general-depth changes, the support expansion and explicit matrix dimensions grow. I did not obtain a bounded-locality refresh operation that prevents this growth while enforcing the computation.
